attributes.purpose: SIEM add-on: the Splunk indexes an environment keeps logs in (searchable and archived retention), its detections as scheduled saved searches, Universal Forwarder inputs placed by Ansible; read back from the opsdir_ciam app's .conf files (round trip) and the management API (read-only collector).

attributes.description: A SIEM as a log destination (milestone 6.2e, decision 3046). Core: a ciamLogDestination of kind siem-index keeps logs searchable (ciamRetentionDays) and in all, archive included (ciamTotalRetentionDays, 710); check_logs holds the total to the route's obligation (archived-only action); a detection is a ciamAlarmBinding naming the SIEM index it searches (ciamLogDestinationRole) with its search in ciamMetric, rendered with the rule's count-per-window condition (alarms.detection_specs / detection_condition; cloud alarm_specs leave detections out); domains/observability/siem check_siem (lost/broken detections, legal hold on a SIEM); contract Adapter.siem_indexes + Services.siem_keeper (a provider adapter leaves a destination another adapter keeps to it) and connectors.observability.siem_check (a SIEM index nothing keeps); log-routes report per environment with searchable and total days. Splunk: opsdir-adapter-splunk (stack role siem) renders the opsdir_ciam app's indexes.conf (frozenTimePeriodInSecs, archiver.*) and savedsearches.conf, Universal Forwarder inputs.conf per role and install root as HostFiles (Ansible places them), forwarding (outputs.conf) a render note for the Splunk team; reads back its confs (round trip) and the REST API's indexes and saved searches (read-only bearer collector). Sentinel: opsdir-adapter-azure on a siem-index whose ref is a Log Analytics workspace (onboarding, analytics rules, table total retention), read back.

attributes.description: Milestone 104 (6.2e; read it and proposal 3024). A SIEM as a log destination kind: render the SIEM-side inputs/forwarding from log routes, detections from alert rules, and read the SIEM's retention (and detections) back against obligations. STEP 1 (now, before vendor facts): survey (AIMFP DB first) the observability domain (ciamLogRoute, ciamLogDestination, ciamAuditTrail, ciamAlertRule/AlarmBinding, ciamEventStream, retention obligations, legal hold, log collection checks/reports), how each cloud renders log routing today (aws/azure/gcp observability + log routing, prometheus rules), and draft the design. STEP 2: the master sends the Codex research (Splunk HEC/forwarder/indexes/retention REST/saved searches, Sentinel DCR/Logs Ingestion/table retention/analytics rules, Elastic, Sigma/OCSF/ECS, government clouds) as a file path; then escalate the design (kind decision, recommendation first): which SIEMs first (adapter packages, e.g. opsdir-adapter-splunk / Sentinel inside the Azure adapter or its own), neutral model (reuse destination kinds; RESERVED core numbers 710-719, classes 149-150), render outputs, the retention/detection read-back (importer + read-only collector), planner check/report, showcase story (fixtures, no live calls). Build after the answer. Rules 2991 + 3002. Boundary: core observability domain, new SIEM adapter package(s), the cloud adapters' observability/log-routing files only where a SIEM destination must be wired, docs, examples/showcase (ids CHG-2049+, B49+/A150+, data file 28+), tests. NOT the pki domain, cyberark/vault adapters, governance credential schemes, live.py (worker on task 528), NOT infrastructure/network firewall parts or the panos adapter (worker on task 529).
